research_question: What is the effect of skin care interventions (such as emollients) applied during infancy, compared with standard skin care or no skin care intervention, on the risk of developing eczema by 1 to 3 years of age in infants aged 12 months or younger?
control_label: Standard skin care or no intervention
outcome_description: Cumulative incidence or risk of developing atopic dermatitis / eczema diagnosed by 1 to 3 years of age
positive_direction: A positive effect indicates a higher rate or risk of eczema in the skin care intervention group, whereas a negative effect indicates a reduced risk of eczema (protective effect of the intervention)
search_queries: infant emollient skin care eczema trial controlled
infancy skin care moisturiser atopic dermatitis prevention trial outcome
emollients neonates infants eczema incidence comparison controlled
inclusion_criteria: Empirical studies involving infants aged 12 months or younger receiving a prophylactic skin care intervention (such as emollients or moisturizers) compared with standard care or no intervention
Reports quantitative outcome data on the occurrence, incidence, or risk of eczema or atopic dermatitis by 1 to 3 years of age
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, commentaries, editorials, and theoretical papers are excluded)
No comparison between an infant skin care intervention and a control condition (standard care or no intervention)
No quantitative outcome data reported that can produce an effect size (such as incidence counts, proportions, risk ratios, or odds ratios)
Completely unrelated to infant skin care interventions or eczema / atopic dermatitis outcomes
moderators_to_extract: Infant baseline atopic risk (general population vs. high risk with atopic family history)
Type and formulation of skin care intervention (emollient cream, ointment, bath additive)
Age of infant at intervention initiation
Frequency and duration of intervention application
Age at outcome assessment (e.g., 12, 24, or 36 months)
